root_idea.summary: A root centered on fineness or a gap between things: what is narrow, interstitial, penetrated, or left open.
root_idea.development: From spaces and interstices come meanings of passing through, inserting or fastening, being amid something, and friendship conceived as intimate interpenetration; fineness also yields meanings of leanness, narrow paths, and deficiency or need.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is the established noun خَلِيل and appears as both singular and plural.
خِلَال has distinct Quranic spatial and relational uses.
خُلَّة is a distinct Quranic noun meaning intimate friendship.

senses.definition: A close, true, or intimate friend.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person bound by exceptionally sincere or intimate friendship; in the Quran it is used of Abraham as God's خليل and of a close friend. The plural form أَخِلَّاءُ is also attested.

senses.definition: Interstices, intervening spaces, or the midst of something; within or among.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for spaces between or within things, including the midst of people, houses, or clouds. Quranic contextual renderings include “within,” “amid,” and “in the midst.”
In the construction لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خِلَالٌ, it denotes friendship or mutual befriending that cannot secure a benefit in the Hereafter; the form is also analyzed as a plural in this usage.

senses.definition: True, intimate, or sincere friendship and affection.
senses.usage_conditions: A relational noun for a deep bond or intimate affection; in the Quran it occurs in the expression لا خُلَّةٌ, denying the availability of such a bond as a means of securing benefit in the Hereafter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become lean, spare, or emaciated as the flesh diminishes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I use describing reduced flesh or bodily leanness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To miss or fail to find something; of a camel, to miss its pasture and become lean.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object or pasture is introduced with مِنْ in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become poor, needy, or in want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person who has entered a state of need.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce, perforate, or transfix something or someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be done with a spear, arrow, or other piercing implement; the cited usage includes repeated piercing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit a young camel's tongue and insert a pin to prevent it from suckling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized husbandry practice intended to stop suckling and thereby cause the young camel to become lean.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pin or fasten the edges of a garment or tent with a pointed stick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action joins or secures two edges by means of a خِلَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move camels to pasture of the kind called خُلَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pasture-management expression, contrasted with pasture called حَمْض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To particularize or specify, as opposed to making something general.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the contrast عَمَّ وَخَلَّ, “included generally and specified particularly.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick or extract material from between the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is food residue, removed with a toothpick or similar implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate or make something pass through its interstices.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes separating hair with a comb and causing water to flow between the beard hairs or fingers during ablution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill the interstices of masonry with lime or mortar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A constructional use referring to the gaps between stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To inspect plants or fruit individually and replace those that have not grown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of cucumbers, melons, and similar cultivated produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become sour, acidic, spoiled, or changed into vinegar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use of beverages, expressed juice, or wine; some authorities restrict or disallow particular variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a beverage, must, or similar liquid into vinegar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use alongside the intransitive sense of becoming sour or vinegary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To preserve or pickle unripe dates and other produce with vinegar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited procedure includes sunning the produce, sprinkling it with vinegar, and placing it in a jar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall short, be remiss, neglect an obligation, or fail to fulfill a compact or promise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with بِـ for the matter in which one falls short; includes neglect of belief, confession, works, promises, and compacts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become absent from, leave, abandon, or quit a place or station.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of abandoning an appointed military position or becoming absent from people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a frontier or border post to be held by a small body of troops.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative administrative or military construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to want or need something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in questions such as مَا أَخَلَّكَ إِلَى هَذَا, “what caused you to need this?”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to pasture upon خُلَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pasture-related use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a specialized usage, to take from the front.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A marked, assumed tropical usage contrasted with taking from behind; it is retained as a specialized lexical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm tree, to produce defective fruit or dates in the stage called خَلَال.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources record contrary descriptions of the fruit, so the entry preserves both the defective-fruit and named-stage usages without treating them as a single precise botanical diagnosis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter, pass through, or penetrate the interstices or spaces within something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of moving among people, through houses or sand, and figuratively of an admonition penetrating the heart; it also supports expressions meaning “without interruption.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of rain, to be confined to particular places rather than being general.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use describing localized rainfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or pick dates remaining among the roots of palm branches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to dates left after the fruit clusters have been cut.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act together as friends or to associate in mutual friendship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI expression used of several people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have or develop interstices, breaks, chinks, or gaps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The concrete primary use describes a thing in which spaces or breaks have appeared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become shaky, loose, disordered, defective, weak, or unsound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of things, affairs, constitutions, minds, or states that have deteriorated or become disordered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become lean, meagre, or emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a body or person whose flesh has diminished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be wanted or needed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with إِلَى; the passive expression may mean that someone or something has become needed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To serve together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct, sparsely attested social usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have or be confined in pasture of the kind called خُلَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a place containing such pasture or of camels confined to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put an anklet or anklets on a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II use referring to the ornament خَلْخَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take the flesh from a bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized extraction use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on an anklet or anklets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or intransitive use referring to a woman adorning herself with an anklet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment or cloth, to become old and worn out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vinegar: sour or acidified juice, especially from grapes or dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry also records medicinal and culinary uses and the idiom خَلٌّ وَلَا خَمْرٌ, whose value polarity varies by dialectal interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of salty, sour, or bitter plant or pasture, contrasted with خُلَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical and pastoral term with variation in the precise plant class included.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or passage through or between tracts of sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote a sandy route, including one through heaped or separated sands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oblong tract of sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographic use distinct from the route through sand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vein in the neck or back communicating with the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slit, rent, or opening in a garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete opening in woven material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old, worn, thin, or streaked garment or cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used adjectivally of a garment that has become worn or thin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird with no feathers or only a few feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive noun or epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lean, meagre, or emaciated person or camel; in a contrary usage, fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources explicitly record both opposed applications, so the contrast is retained rather than resolved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young camel in its second or third year.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A camel-age designation, also used of the corresponding female; one cited comparison emphasizes smallness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cautery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road between two roads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial noun for a route or passage between routes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small penetrating hole, perforation, or gap.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a breach in a reed booth or similar structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vacant place or gap left by a person who has died.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in supplications asking that the deceased person's absence be supplied or repaired.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The interval between a piercer and the thing pierced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression associated with striking or thrusting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Want, poverty, need, straitness, or difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote a pressing need that requires being supplied or relieved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quality, disposition, habit, or customary practice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's characteristic nature or conduct; its plural is خِلَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An isolated or elevated tract of sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources include both a separate sandy tract and a term compared with هَضْبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine, especially sour or altered wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources differ over whether the word denotes wine generally, sour wine, or wine changed for the worse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sweet pasture, herbage, or trees that are not of the salty or sour kind called حَمْض.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pastoral and botanical noun; usage varies over whether it includes trees, shrubs, or land without herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ease, repose, freedom from trouble, or ampleness of circumstances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from pleasant pasture; it may also be contrasted figuratively with hardship or death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Acid or sour leaven or ferment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized food-related noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The leather covering or lining of a sword scabbard; also a bow thong or decorated piece of skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word covers related leather or skin components, including a thong at the curved end of a bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A flaw, defect, imperfection, deficiency, looseness, or disorder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of an affair, thing, war, people, or opinion that lacks compactness or soundness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical usage recorded without further constructional restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Green dates in the stage called بَلَح.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or dialectal noun with a singulative in ـة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An accident or change in a sweet substance that makes its flavor acidic or sour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized result noun related to the souring of beverages or foods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pin, skewer, toothpick, or similar implement used to pierce, fasten, or clear an interstice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes an iron or wooden piercing tool, a garment pin, a meat skewer, a camel-tongue pin, and a toothpick.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perforated or transpierced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival use distinct from خَلِيل meaning a friend.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poor, needy, or in want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal or adjectival use connected with the semantic notion of a gap or need, but distinct from the friendship noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who advises, counsels, or acts sincerely and faithfully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a trustworthy adviser.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare anatomical or lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The liver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use, including a named sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scattered ripe dates remaining among the roots of palm branches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to fruit left after the main clusters have been cut.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food residue that comes out from between the teeth when they are picked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the remains removed by tooth-picking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of vinegar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pertaining to or pasturing upon خُلَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of a camel or camels and in expressions concerning the change between pasture types.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized geographic description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman's anklet or pair of anklets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A well-known women's ornament; variant forms and plural patterns are recorded in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having gaps or interstices; uncompact or incoherent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited adjectival forms can be applied to an army as well as to other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most poor, needy, or in need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative derived from the use of أَخَلَّ إِلَيْهِ meaning “to need.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land abounding in خُلَّة and lacking the pasture called حَمْض.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pastoral description of land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of the leg where an anklet is worn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to the leg of a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemently thirsty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak or unsound; in a defective or disordered state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of an affair or condition that lacks soundness.

cautions: The Quranic form خِلَال has both a spatial/interstitial sense and a friendship sense; these are separated because the Quran uses them in materially different constructions.

One Lane passage uses an older citation notation for a friendship expression and reports a location not reproduced as a modern QAC occurrence. The friendship sense is retained on the basis of the lexical explanation and the independently supplied QAC/Mufradat evidence, without treating that Lane notation as a modern verse key.
